R: India has limited domestic manufacturing capacity for electrolysers and their key components.
x: Both are true: India still imports most electrolysers because domestic manufacturing capacity is small, which is why import dependence is a challenge for green hydrogen.

R: Most NCDs are chronic, lifestyle-linked diseases that are cheaper to prevent or detect early than to treat at a late stage.
x: Both are true: since NCDs are chronic and lifestyle-linked, prevention and early screening cost less than late curative care, so the health system must shift towards them.

A: In August 2026 heatwaves and lightning became eligible for SDRF assistance.
R: They were added to the notified list of disasters (12 to 14) for 2026-31 on the 16th Finance Commission's recommendation.
x: Both are true: SDRF assistance is given only for notified disasters, and heatwaves and lightning were added to that list on the 16th Finance Commission's recommendation.

R: A dealer can claim input tax credit only on invoices showing tax paid by the seller, so each buyer has an incentive to demand proper tax invoices.
x: Both are true: because input tax credit depends on the seller's invoice, buyers check sellers along the chain, which is why VAT is called self-enforcing.

R: Unlike the remedy under Article 32, the remedy under Article 226 is not itself a Fundamental Right.
x: Both are true: Article 32 is a Fundamental Right, but Article 226 is not, so a High Court may refuse writ relief - its writ power is discretionary.

R: The Government of India Act 1858 gave the Governor-General the additional title of Viceroy, the direct representative of the Crown.
x: Both are true: the 1858 Act made the Governor-General the Viceroy, the Crown's representative, so Canning became the first Viceroy.

R: Vulnerable developing countries had long demanded finance for climate impacts that mitigation and adaptation cannot prevent.
x: Both are true: COP27 set up loss and damage funding arrangements in response to the long-standing demand of vulnerable developing countries.

R: The Act shares wage costs between the Centre and the States in the ratio 60:40.
x: Both are true: VB-G RAM G has 60:40 Centre-State wage sharing, so the States bear 40% of the wage cost.

R: At the Fourth Council the Buddhists differed over new doctrines such as Bodhisattva worship and image worship of the Buddha.
x: Both are true: the split into Mahayana and Hinayana came from the doctrinal differences (Bodhisattva and image worship) at the Fourth Council.

R: During La Nina, a cooler central-east Pacific and stronger trade winds strengthen the Walker circulation, favouring rising air and rain over India.
x: Both are true: the stronger Walker circulation during La Nina favours convection over the Indian region, so La Nina years usually bring a stronger monsoon.

R: GACSA is a voluntary alliance in which members decide their own actions.
x: Both are true: since GACSA is a voluntary, non-binding alliance, membership creates no binding obligations.

A: The AP IT (Electronic Service Delivery) Rules, 2011 were framed under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
R: The IT Act, as amended in 2008, empowers governments to deliver services electronically, including through authorised service providers.
x: Both are true: the 2008 amendment of the IT Act gave governments the power to provide electronic service delivery, under which AP framed its 2011 Rules.

R: On the flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv flight of 30 September 2026 he protected the passengers when attacked by a fellow pilot, saving 174 lives.
x: Both are true: Israel gave him its Presidential Award for Civilian Heroism for protecting the passengers and saving 174 lives on the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight.

R: It contains a section on rajaniti, Krishnadevaraya's advice on how a king should govern.
x: Both are true: the rajaniti (polity) section of Amuktamalyada is why it is valued as a source on statecraft.

A: Under ABDM, a patient's health records held at different hospitals can be linked together.
R: Each citizen can get an ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) number, a unique health ID to which records are linked.
x: Both are true: the ABHA health ID is the common key that lets a patient's records at different facilities be linked under ABDM.

A: Jayapa is remembered by the title 'Senani' (commander).
R: He was Gaja Sahini, the head of the elephant corps of Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
x: Both are true: as Gaja Sahini, commander of the elephant force, Jayapa was a military chief - hence the title Senani.

A: Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India.
R: The Charter Act, 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
x: Both are true: Bentinck, then Governor-General of Bengal, became the first Governor-General of India because the 1833 Act redesignated the post.

A: West Bengal has the largest mangrove cover among Indian States.
R: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, lies in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta of West Bengal.
x: Both are true: the Sundarbans give West Bengal the largest mangrove cover in India.

A: Red sanders can be exported only with CITES export permits.
R: Red sanders is listed in Appendix II of CITES.
x: Both are true: Appendix II species may be traded only with export permits, and red sanders is in Appendix II.

R: Section 6(2) of the RTI Act says an applicant need not give any reason for seeking information.
x: Both are true: the Act itself bars asking for reasons, so the Madras High Court's remark that applicants should state reasons had to be withdrawn.

R: Article 246(4) empowers Parliament to make laws for any part of India not included in a State, even on State List matters.
x: Both are true: Article 246(4) is the basis of Parliament's power to legislate on State List subjects for Union Territories.

A: Satendra Singh Lohia's Cook Strait swim was a crossing between New Zealand's North and South Islands.
R: The Cook Strait separates New Zealand's North Island from its South Island.
x: Both are true: because the Cook Strait lies between New Zealand's two main islands, crossing it means swimming from one island to the other.

R: Makrana in Rajasthan is famous for its high-quality white marble quarries.
x: Both are true: the fine white marble quarried at Makrana was used for the Taj Mahal and the Victoria Memorial.

R: Under zero MDR, merchants pay no charge on RuPay debit card and BHIM-UPI transactions, so the processing cost falls on banks and payment providers.
x: Both are true: with no merchant discount rate, the cost of processing is borne by banks and payment system providers (partly offset by the government incentive).

A: Article 370 is now inoperative.
R: In August 2019 the President, acting under Article 370(3), declared that its clauses had ceased to operate.
x: Both are true: Article 370(3) let the President declare it inoperative by notification, which was done in August 2019.

R: Andhra Pradesh is India's largest producer of Virginia flue-cured (FCV) tobacco, the main export variety.
x: Both are true: as the largest producer of export-grade FCV tobacco, AP ranks first in India's tobacco exports.

A: The 16th India-Japan Annual Summit (July 2026) was Sanae Takaichi's first official visit to India.
R: Sanae Takaichi became Japan's Prime Minister only on 21 October 2025.
x: Both are true: having become PM in October 2025, Takaichi made her first official India visit for the 16th Annual Summit in July 2026.

R: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami struck India's coast without any warning system in place.
x: Both are true: the lack of warning in the 2004 tsunami led India to set up the Tsunami Early Warning Centre at INCOIS, opened in 2007.

R: The National Literacy Mission aimed at adult literacy through area-specific, time-bound, volunteer-based campaigns.
x: Both are true: NLM's strategy of time-bound, volunteer-based area campaigns took the form of the Total Literacy Campaign.

R: Uniper is a German energy company.
x: Both are true: since the buyer, Uniper, is German, the Kakinada green ammonia supply is described as India's first green energy export to Europe.

R: He resigned because the Hindu Code Bill he had drafted was held up in Parliament.
x: Both are true: Ambedkar resigned in September 1951 mainly over the stalling of the Hindu Code Bill.

R: Section 15Z of the SEBI Act, 1992 allows an appeal against a SAT order to the Supreme Court on a question of law arising from it.
x: Both are true: the SEBI Act limits appeals from SAT to the Supreme Court to questions of law.

A: Later Vedic people were able to clear the forests of the Ganga plain for farming.
R: Iron tools spread in North India between about 1000 and 600 BC.
x: Both are true: iron axes and ploughshares, spreading from about 1000 BC, made forest clearance and farming in the Ganga plain possible.

A: India's nuclear doctrine requires a survivable nuclear force.
R: Under No First Use, India must be able to retaliate massively after absorbing a first strike.
x: Both are true: as India will not strike first, its deterrent depends on forces that survive a first strike to retaliate.

A: Punjab was annexed by the British in 1849.
R: The Sikhs were defeated in the Second Anglo-Sikh War, which included the Battles of Chillianwala and Gujrat (1849).
x: Both are true: the Sikh defeat in the Second Anglo-Sikh War led Dalhousie to annex Punjab in 1849.

R: The RBI's priority-sector guidelines list micro, small and medium enterprises as a priority-sector category.
x: Both are true: since MSMEs are a priority-sector category, bank loans to them (meeting the conditions) count as priority-sector lending.

A: The February 2019 AP budget was a vote on account.
R: In an election year a State seeks approval only for interim expenditure under Article 206, leaving the full budget to the new government.
x: Both are true: 2019 was an election year, so AP passed a vote on account under Article 206.

R: The Yarlung Tsangpo flows into India as the Siang/Brahmaputra, so a dam upstream can affect water flows downstream.
x: Both are true: the Yarlung Tsangpo is the upper Brahmaputra, so India, as the downstream State, is concerned about the dam.

A: Nellore and Chittoor became part of the Madras Presidency in 1801.
R: By the Carnatic Treaty of 1801 with Nawab Azim-ud-Daula, the Company annexed the Carnatic districts.
x: Both are true: Nellore and Chittoor were Carnatic districts, annexed by the 1801 Carnatic Treaty and merged into the Madras Presidency.

R: The RBI pays for the dollars it buys by creating rupees, which adds to the reserves of banks.
x: Both are true: buying dollars injects newly created rupees (base money), so domestic money supply expands.

R: Biomining recovers reusable materials such as soil-like fines, plastics and metals from legacy waste.
x: Both are true: by recovering materials for reuse and freeing dumpsite land, biomining supports the circular economy.

R: Under the 2008 India-specific Safeguards Agreement, imported nuclear fuel can be used only in reactors placed under IAEA safeguards.
x: Both are true: the safeguards agreement after the NSG waiver requires reactors using imported uranium to be under IAEA safeguards.

A: The SIPRI Yearbook 2026 lists India among the nine nuclear-armed states.
R: India had about 190 nuclear warheads in early 2026.
x: Both are true: SIPRI counts India as nuclear-armed because it holds about 190 warheads.

R: At the 1944 Salem conference, E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar), then its president, renamed the Justice Party as the Dravidar Kazhagam.
x: Both are true: Periyar's resolution at Salem (1944) transformed the Justice Party into the DK.

R: Rising farm wages and a tighter labour market, as workers move to non-farm jobs, make labour-saving machines profitable.
x: Both are true: private investment goes into mechanisation in response to rising wages and labour shortages.

R: The Hathnora skull belongs to the Middle Pleistocene and is older than any other hominin fossil found in India.
x: Both are true: its Middle Pleistocene age makes the Narmada Man the earliest human fossil in India.

R: DAP 2020 aims at indigenisation, and IDDM items must be indigenously designed, developed and manufactured with at least 50% indigenous content.
x: Both are true: DAP 2020's goal of Aatmanirbharta makes Buy (Indian-IDDM), the most indigenous category, the most preferred.

R: At high latitudes the Sun's path meets the horizon at a low, oblique angle, so it takes longer to sink 18 degrees below the horizon.
x: Both are true: the oblique path of the Sun at high latitudes lengthens twilight (whereas at the Equator it is short).

A: K.C. Wheare described the Indian Constitution as quasi-federal.
R: The Constitution gives the Centre overriding powers, such as emergency provisions and the appointment of Governors.
x: Both are true: the strong unitary features in a federal set-up led Wheare to call India quasi-federal.

R: The Kakatiya army needed cavalry horses, which could not be bred well in the Deccan and were brought by sea through ports such as Motupalli.
x: Both are true: the demand for cavalry horses that the Deccan could not supply made Arabian horses a key import.

R: Neighbourhood First gives priority to relations with India's immediate South Asian neighbours.
x: Both are true: inviting SAARC leaders to the 2014 swearing-in reflected the priority given to neighbours under Neighbourhood First.

A: The Raghupathi Venkaiah Award honours lifetime contribution to Telugu cinema.
R: It is named after Raghupathi Venkaiah Naidu, regarded as the father of Telugu cinema.
x: Both are true: the lifetime Nandi honour bears the name of Raghupathi Venkaiah Naidu, the father of Telugu cinema.

R: No bilingual inscription has been found, and most Harappan inscriptions are very short.
x: Both are true: without a bilingual key and with very short texts, the script cannot be deciphered.

A: Article 48A is not enforceable in a court of law.
R: It is a Directive Principle of State Policy, and under Article 37 the Directive Principles are non-justiciable.
x: Both are true: Article 48A is a DPSP, and DPSPs are not enforceable in courts (Article 37).

A: Pumped storage plants help balance a grid with variable solar and wind power.
R: They pump water uphill with surplus power and generate electricity by releasing it at times of peak demand.
x: Both are true: by storing surplus power and releasing it at peak, pumped storage balances variable renewable supply.

R: SDG target 3.3 calls for ending epidemics such as AIDS, TB and malaria and combating hepatitis by 2030.
x: Both are true: hepatitis is part of SDG 3.3, so India's 2030 hepatitis target aligns with it.

R: The subtropical high-pressure belts have clear skies, high evaporation and low rainfall.
x: Both are true: high evaporation and little rain in the subtropical highs make surface salinity highest there.

R: While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, the Speaker does not preside and sits as an ordinary member.
x: Both are true: since he does not preside then (Article 181), the Speaker votes in the first instance like any member.

R: Article 345 lets a State Legislature adopt by law any language used in the State as its official language.
x: Both are true: the AP Official Languages Act, 1966 was enacted under Article 345 to make Telugu the official language.

R: It is spread over about 1,666 acres with studios, sets and production facilities in one place.
x: Both are true: its size (about 1,666 acres) and integrated facilities make Ramoji Film City the world's largest film studio complex per Guinness.

R: Poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) had been the central slogan of Indira Gandhi's 1971 campaign, and the Plan was drafted to give it effect.
x: Both are true: the Fifth Plan reflected the 1971 Garibi Hatao commitment, focusing on poverty removal and self-reliance.

R: It is a US-led coalition of partner countries building trusted technology supply chains with less reliance on coercive suppliers.
x: Both are true: as a coalition for trusted supply chains, Pax Silica aims to secure supply of critical minerals, semiconductors and AI infrastructure.

R: He did extensive research on cotton, especially Cambodia cotton.
x: Both are true: his work on cotton varieties earned him the name Patti (cotton) Venkayya.

A: Article 350B was inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956.
R: The States Reorganisation Commission recommended a Special Officer to safeguard linguistic minorities.
x: Both are true: Article 350B (Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities) was added in 1956 on the SRC's recommendation.

R: The Great Indian Bustard is a heavy bird with poor frontal vision that cannot turn quickly to avoid overhead lines.
x: Both are true: its weak frontal vision and heavy flight make the bustard collide with power lines, its biggest threat.

A: India's rank of 94th in the Sustainable Development Report 2026 is its best ever.
R: India's previous best was 99th in SDR 2025, when it first entered the top 100.
x: Both are true: improving on its earlier best of 99th, India's 94th place in SDR 2026 is its best ever.

A: Many Census Towns are still governed by rural local bodies.
R: A Census Town is identified only by demographic criteria (5,000+ population, 400+ per sq km, 75%+ male non-farm workers), not by a statutory notification.
x: Both are true: Census Towns are not statutory urban bodies, so many remain under panchayats.

R: Under No First Use, India pledges never to initiate a nuclear strike and keeps its weapons only to deter and retaliate.
x: Both are true: the NFU pledge limits Indian nuclear use to retaliation against a nuclear attack.

R: Its high clay content gives black soil great moisture-retaining capacity.
x: Both are true: because black soil holds moisture, it needs little irrigation.

A: Unemployment rates under the Current Weekly Status are generally higher than under the usual status (UPSS).
R: CWS uses a short 7-day reference period, which captures seasonal and intermittent unemployment that the 365-day usual status misses.
x: Both are true: the short reference week picks up temporary unemployment, so CWS rates exceed UPSS rates.

A: Doordarshan's terrestrial television needed a dense network of ground transmitters.
R: Terrestrial TV signals travel by line of sight, so each transmitter covers only a limited area.
x: Both are true: the line-of-sight range of each transmitter is why a wide network of transmitters was needed.

A: Andhra Pradesh's best pillar rank in the India Justice Report 2025 was in Police.
R: In IJR 2025 AP ranked 2nd in Police, 4th in Prisons and 5th in Judiciary and Legal Aid.
x: Both are true: of AP's pillar ranks (2nd, 4th, 5th, 5th), Police (2nd) is the best.

R: At 100% relative humidity no water evaporates from the wet bulb, so there is no evaporative cooling.
x: Both are true: with saturated air there is no evaporation, so the wet bulb reads the same as the dry bulb.

R: APCO introduced computerised billing and sold handloom products through e-commerce platforms.
x: Both are true: APCO won the SKOCH Award-2025 for these digitisation steps in the handloom sector.

A: Workers registered on e-Shram can access several central schemes through one portal.
R: The e-Shram One-Stop Solution (2024) links 15 central schemes to the portal.
x: Both are true: the One-Stop Solution integrates 15 central schemes into e-Shram, giving one-point access.

A: The modern Perini Shivatandavam is a reconstruction of a dance that had died out.
R: Nataraja Ramakrishna revived it from Jayapa's Nritta Ratnavali and the Ramappa and Thousand Pillar temple sculptures.
x: Both are true: Perini survives today because Nataraja Ramakrishna rebuilt it from the text and temple sculptures.

R: They give rules, including the Baudhayana (Pythagorean) theorem, for building fire altars of exact shapes and sizes.
x: Both are true: the altar-building rules in the Sulbasutras show Vedic skill in geometry.

A: Derozio was dismissed from Hindu College in 1831.
R: The orthodox managers of the college objected to his radical teaching, which led students to question religion and custom.
x: Both are true: orthodox opposition to his rationalist influence on students caused his dismissal.

R: Higher domestic spending raises incomes and demand, including demand for imports, rather than raising exports.
x: Both are true: since such spending adds to import demand and does not boost exports, it does not correct a BoP deficit.

A: TOPCon solar cells are more efficient than conventional PERC cells.
R: A tunnel oxide passivated contact layer reduces recombination losses at the rear of the cell.
x: Both are true: lower recombination losses from the passivated contact give TOPCon cells higher efficiency.

R: Guru Arjan included in the Adi Granth the compositions of saints whose nirguna bhakti matched Sikh teachings.
x: Both are true: Namdev's nirguna bhakti agreed with Sikh teachings, so his hymns were included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

A: Roman coins have been found in large numbers in the Deccan and South India.
R: Indo-Roman trade brought Roman gold and silver in exchange for Indian pepper, textiles and gems.
x: Both are true: Roman payment in gold and silver for Indian goods explains the hoards of Roman coins.

A: Families covered by the Visakhapatnam City Police health insurance scheme did not pay the first year's premium.
R: The first-year premium was paid from the police fund.
x: Both are true: since the police fund paid the first-year premium, the families paid nothing that year.

A: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 protects women even from abuse that is not physical.
R: It defines domestic violence to include sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse besides physical abuse.
x: Both are true: the wide definition of domestic violence extends protection to non-physical abuse.

R: The Supreme Court reads Article 21 broadly as a right to live with dignity, which today requires equal access to digital services.
x: Both are true: the dignity-based reading of Article 21 is why digital access is held to be part of it.

R: NSG commandos wear black uniforms and a black cat insignia.
x: Both are true: their black dress and black cat insignia earned the NSG the name 'Black Cats'.

R: Cesses and surcharges are not shared with the States, so the Union keeps all of that revenue.
x: Both are true: revenue raised outside the divisible pool stays with the Union, widening the gap between States' revenues and responsibilities.

A: Only the Crew Module of Gaganyaan's Orbital Module returns to Earth.
R: The Service Module, which gives propulsion and power in orbit, is jettisoned before re-entry.
x: Both are true: the Service Module separates before re-entry, so only the Crew Module comes back.

R: The FCRA applies to every association or NGO that receives foreign contribution, whatever its form of registration.
x: Both are true: since FCRA covers all NGOs regardless of legal form, a Section 8 company also needs FCRA registration or prior permission.

R: He was a great wrestler, which is what 'Mamalla' means.
x: Both are true: Narasimhavarman I was called Mamalla (great wrestler) for his wrestling skill.

R: Fiscal policy is the government's policy on its revenue and expenditure, and public debt finances the gap between them.
x: Both are true: as fiscal policy covers revenue, spending and their financing, it includes taxation, expenditure and public debt.

R: It was launched under the PM Garib Kalyan Package to give free foodgrains to NFSA beneficiaries during the COVID-19 lockdown.
x: Both are true: PMGKAY was started in 2020 as COVID-19 relief.

R: It includes large recurring items such as interest payments, subsidies, salaries, pensions and grants to States.
x: Both are true: these large recurring items make revenue expenditure the biggest block of the Union Budget.

A: West Godavari had the lowest multidimensional poverty (2.42%) among AP's old 13 districts.
R: West Godavari is a prosperous, canal-irrigated district of the Godavari delta.
x: Both are true: its prosperous irrigated delta economy explains its lowest MPI headcount (2.42%).

R: It ranks States on their support for startups, encouraging them to compete in improving their policies.
x: Both are true: by ranking States against each other, DPIIT's ranking promotes competitive federalism.

A: Earth Day (22 April) was first observed in 1970 in the USA.
R: It grew out of US Senator Gaylord Nelson's call for a nationwide environmental teach-in.
x: Both are true: Gaylord Nelson's teach-in idea led to the first Earth Day in the USA in 1970.

A: The AP Economic Development Board has a statutory basis.
R: It functions under the APEDB Act, 2018.
x: Both are true: APEDB is statutory because it was set up under the APEDB Act, 2018.

A: B.S. Guha recognised the Negrito as a racial element in India's population.
R: He found Negrito traits such as frizzly hair among tribes like the Kadar and Irula of South India and the Andamanese.
x: Both are true: the Negrito traits he observed in these tribes led Guha to list the Negrito as a separate group.

A: The National Renewal Fund (1992) was set up as a safety net for workers.
R: Industrial restructuring under the 1991 New Industrial Policy threatened the jobs of workers in sick and loss-making units.
x: Both are true: the NRF was created to protect workers hit by restructuring after the 1991 policy.

A: China's trade with Africa is about twice India's.
R: China's trade with Africa is over $200 billion, while India's is about $100 billion.
x: Both are true: about $200 billion against India's $100 billion makes China's Africa trade roughly double.

A: The Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm conventions are run together under a 'synergies' arrangement.
R: The three conventions, all dealing with hazardous chemicals and wastes, share one joint secretariat under UNEP.
x: Both are true: the shared joint secretariat (UNEP) is the basis of their joint working.

A: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Azad shot Saunders in December 1928.
R: They sought to avenge Lala Lajpat Rai's death from injuries received in the police lathi charge at Lahore.
x: Both are true: Saunders was shot to avenge Lajpat Rai's death after the lathi charge on the anti-Simon procession.

R: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, and cutting its demand for grants shows it has lost the House's support.
x: Both are true: under collective responsibility, losing a cut motion means losing the Lok Sabha's confidence.

R: The British constitution evolved over centuries through conventions, statutes and judicial decisions rather than being framed by a constituent body.
x: Both are true: because it grew gradually, Britain has no single written constitution.

A: In India, Parliament alone can make laws on subjects not in any of the three Lists.
R: Article 248 and Entry 97 of the Union List vest residuary powers in Parliament.
x: Both are true: Article 248 and Entry 97 give Parliament the residuary power.

A: Plateaus are often called tablelands.
R: A plateau is an elevated area with a broad, flat top that rises sharply above the surrounding land.
x: Both are true: its flat top and steep sides make a plateau look like a table.

A: Rice yields in Andhra Pradesh are above the national average.
R: Much of AP's rice is grown under assured canal irrigation in the Godavari and Krishna deltas.
x: Both are true: assured delta irrigation raises AP's rice yields above the national average.

R: Under parliamentary sovereignty, an Act of the UK Parliament is the supreme law.
x: Both are true: because Parliament is sovereign in the UK, courts cannot declare its Acts void.

A: The water of the Luni becomes saline in its lower course.
R: In its lower course the Luni flows over salt-rich arid land, where high evaporation concentrates the salts.
x: Both are true: the salt-bearing soils and high evaporation of the arid region make its lower course saline.

A: The Imad Shahi kingdom of Berar was one of the five successor states of the Bahmani kingdom.
R: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk, the Bahmani governor of Berar, declared independence in 1490.
x: Both are true: Berar became a Bahmani successor state when its governor broke away in 1490.

A: The term of the Attorney General is not fixed by the Constitution.
R: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President.
x: Both are true: as he serves at the President's pleasure (Article 76(4)), no fixed term is laid down.

A: UDAN aims to make air travel affordable for common citizens through regional connectivity.
R: Under UDAN, airlines get viability gap funding to keep fares capped on unserved and underserved routes.
x: Both are true: viability gap funding with capped fares is how UDAN makes regional flights affordable.

R: She was elected IOC President in March 2025, succeeding Thomas Bach, and no woman had held the post before.
x: Both are true: her 2025 election to a post never before held by a woman makes Coventry the first woman IOC President.

R: Until its inscription in 2021, no Harappan site in India was on the list; Mohenjo-daro, listed in 1980, is in Pakistan.
x: Both are true: since no Indian Harappan site was listed before 2021, Dholavira became the first.

A: The real political awakening in Andhra came in 1905.
R: The Swadeshi (Vandemataram) movement against the partition of Bengal spread to Andhra that year and drew wide public support.
x: Both are true: the spread of the Vandemataram movement in 1905 marked Andhra's political awakening.

A: As per the India Justice Report 2025, Andhra Pradesh has the highest share of women in its police among States.
R: Women make up 22% of Andhra Pradesh's police force.
x: Both are true: AP's 22% share of women in the police is the highest among States.

A: Nominated members of Parliament take part in the impeachment of the President.
R: Impeachment is a power of Parliament alone, in which all members of both Houses, elected or nominated, take part.
x: Both are true: as impeachment is by the whole Parliament, nominated members also take part (unlike in the election).

R: An NAC is set up by a State government notification for a fast-developing town not yet fit for a municipality, and is not a statutory elected body.
x: Both are true: being created by notification rather than by election, an NAC is entirely nominated.

A: The Theosophical Society's ideas found wide acceptance among educated Hindus.
R: It glorified ancient Hindu religion and philosophy, including the Vedas and Upanishads.
x: Both are true: its praise of ancient Hindu philosophy appealed to educated Hindus.

A: The Guntur no-tax campaign was suspended on 11 February 1922.
R: After the Chauri Chaura incident, Gandhi sent a message to Konda Venkatappayya to suspend it.
x: Both are true: the campaign was suspended on Gandhi's message after Chauri Chaura.

R: In September 2013 the Supreme Court (PUCL v. Union of India) directed the Election Commission to provide a NOTA option.
x: Both are true: NOTA came after the 2013 Supreme Court ruling, so the 2014 Lok Sabha election was the first to use it.

R: Cas9 is an enzyme that, guided by an RNA sequence, cuts DNA at a chosen site.
x: Both are true: Cas9's guided, precise cutting of DNA is what allows genes to be deleted, inserted or altered.

R: In it, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the elected lower House and stays in office only while it has that House's confidence.
x: Both are true: the executive's responsibility to the legislature is why the parliamentary system is called responsible government.

R: Concrete, asphalt and buildings absorb and retain heat, and there is less vegetation for cooling.
x: Both are true: heat-retaining urban surfaces and little vegetation create the urban heat island.

A: Hul Diwas is observed on 30 June.
R: The Santal Hul began on 30 June 1855, when Sidho and Kanho Murmu gathered thousands of Santals at Bhognadih.
x: Both are true: Hul Diwas marks the day the rebellion began at Bhognadih.

A: Deepam-2 benefits families that already have LPG connections.

x: Both are true: since Deepam-2 gives free refills rather than connections, it serves families already connected.
